pr_title: Ensure IMC sessions are logged out at each exit point (#65169)
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Fixes #65169

The atexit hook alone is not sufficient enough to ensure all IMC sessions are close properly. The atexit module is hooked to the exit of the python interpreter and the imc_rest module itself can exit before the interpreter exits.  To fix this, calls to the logout function were added to each point where an exit happens and an IMC session has been established.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
imc_rest

In the past this wasn't needed, so why did this behaviour change?
It means Ansible modules no longer work with atexit? That doesn't seem right.

I have always experienced this issue with imc_rest, all the way back to 2.6. It tends to happen when iterating through failures with plays calling imc_rest multiple times. Considering these lines 

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/modules/remote_management/imc/imc_rest.py#L412
https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/modules/remote_management/imc/imc_rest.py#L427

If I have a play that has more than 4 calls to imc_rest (XMLapi max session has a hard limit at 4 in IMC) before the python interpreter exits, the session limit will be reached and the API will refuse new connections. Its not so much that atexit is not working or has a bug, its just that the session limit is reached because of how many times imc_rest is called.

Talking through this, I think there is an even better way to deal with it and there is an optimization I can put in place so that only one session is needed per play regardless of how many calls to imc_rest are made. Thanks for questioning the changes! I will work that change up and resubmit the PR.

If it does not logout when python exits, then `atexit` is not working. That is the whole point of using `atexit` here, things may fail unexpectedly and we should `logout()` at every exit scenario. So your fix is not fixing all the uses of a working `atexit` and we should be looking at the cause.

Again, the issue is not with atexit, the issue is with multiple calls to imc_rest exhausting the available sessions for the XLMApi. If I call imc_rest 5 times in one play, it tries to create 5 sessions and fails to create the 5th. atexit is only called when the python process is finished, not when an ansible play or module execution is finished.

> I have always experienced this issue with imc_rest, all the way back to 2.6. It tends to happen when iterating through failures with plays calling imc_rest multiple times.

It doesn't make sense, so you are saying that `atexit` does work when it exits successfully, but not when it fails. `atexit` is ignorant of the exit scenario AFAICT.

Are you by any chance running something like Mitogen?

> atexit is only called when the python process is finished, not when an ansible play or module execution is finished.

Oh, right. But then we have a problem when there is an unexpected exit. I guess what we need is a way to hook into the module exit. This would require changes to module_utils to allow this, as the module could not handle this itself.
BTW you can already do multiple calls with a single `imc_rest` call today.

The edge case we are talking through is not something that would come up if you bundle multiple payloads into a single imc_rest call, so thats likely why its hit or miss for some.. In the case where I call imc_rest 5 times in one play, and there are no failures on the first 4 invocations of imc_rest, the 5th call will fail because the previous 4 calls did not clean up their sessions.

For my use case, the more transactional approach to calling imc_rest suits the needs better.

It would be nice if there were some helpers to hook to an exit of a module, but this is a bigger change, and I don't see why adding the logout call to points where the module finishes is bad. The atexit hook is more for cleaning up after unexpected failures, not cleanup after a successful run.

Well, if `atexit` would be working (like before when we did not reuse the python interpreter) it worked fine for all exit scenarios. With this PR there would be 2 calls to `logout()` in some scenarios.
Yup spot on, if each module was invoked in its own interpreter, the issue would not exist. I'll look further into the scenario of multiple calls to logout as well.

I no longer have hardware to test this.
So it would be better if someone else takes over maintainership.

Looking at the code, there have not been any changes between v2.8 and v2.9.
The code uses `atexit` to ensure a `logout()` is performed.
So the code looks correct and should be working fine.

I can only see one potential cornercase where we call `fail_json()` when a cookie is not acquired without performing a `logout()`. But in that case you would get a specific error.

And if there is no cookie, we cannot perform a logout() anyhow.
Maybe there has been a change in how Ansible exits its module runs that causes `atexit` not to work correctly. But we haven't seen this ourselves. This would depend on the use-case.

Also, did you know you can perform many operations in the same call by using multiple documents in the payload? This may simplify your playbook and would be more efficient because there would only be one login and one logout.

There is an example in the documentation for this.
